christianOrgs.name: The Catholic Center at NYU
christianOrgs.blurb: The hub for Catholic life at NYU: daily Mass and the sacraments, student Bible studies, retreats, service projects and social events, plus study and fellowship space that stays open late. Runs separate programming for undergraduates, graduate students and alumni.
christianOrgs.where: 238 Thompson St, New York, NY 10012 — Mon–Fri 11am–9pm, Sat–Sun 1–9pm

christianOrgs.name: InterVarsity Christian Fellowship
christianOrgs.blurb: The All-University InterVarsity chapter — an interdenominational evangelical fellowship with weekly large-group meetings and small-group Bible studies.

christianOrgs.name: Graduate Christian Fellowship
christianOrgs.blurb: An All-University fellowship for graduate and professional students, rather than the undergraduate-focused groups most of this list covers.

christianOrgs.name: NYU Cru
christianOrgs.blurb: NYU's chapter of Cru, an interdenominational campus ministry running weekly meetings, small groups and summer missions.

christianOrgs.name: Asian American Christian Fellowship (AACF)
christianOrgs.blurb: An InterVarsity fellowship centred on the Asian American Christian community at NYU.

christianOrgs.name: Encounter Christian Fellowship
christianOrgs.blurb: A campus fellowship connected to Remnant Church, listed among NYU's religious and spiritual life clubs.

christianOrgs.name: Every Nation Campus
christianOrgs.blurb: The NYU chapter of Every Nation's campus ministry, running Bible studies and discipleship groups.

christianOrgs.name: International Chinese Christian Fellowship
christianOrgs.blurb: A fellowship for Chinese and Chinese-speaking students, with bilingual Bible study and community events.

christianOrgs.name: The Navigators
christianOrgs.blurb: NYU's chapter of The Navigators, a discipleship-focused campus ministry built around one-to-one and small-group Bible study.

christianOrgs.name: Compass Koinonia
christianOrgs.blurb: The NYU counterpart to Columbia's CCK, connected to Compass Fellowship Church.

christianOrgsNote: Only the Catholic Center was confirmed on its own site — nyu.edu's club directory could not be opened when this list was compiled, so every other entry is a name from search results with no contact details attached, and is marked unconfirmed for that reason. The reliable way in is NYU's Global Spiritual Life office, which convenes the chaplains and advisors behind these clubs: spiritual.life@nyu.edu, +1 212 998 4959, 238 Thompson St, 4th Floor. Club officers turn over every year, so ask them for a current contact rather than trusting a handle found online.

startingAnRso.intro: All-University clubs at NYU are registered with the Center for Student Life (CSL) and approved by the Student Activities Board (SAB). A new group is not recognized straight away: it first applies to the New Club Development (NCD) program, completes SAB and CSL training, and puts on a showcase event, and recognition follows from finishing that program. Applications go through NYU Engage and have historically opened in September, with interviews for qualified applicants after the deadline.
requirements: An application to the New Club Development (NCD) program, submitted through NYU Engage — SAB does not recognize All-University clubs outside this program.
At least two club officers: a President and a Treasurer.
A written constitution setting out the club's structure and how it operates.
An interview with SAB after the application deadline, for applicants who qualify.
Completion of the NCD training run by SAB and CSL, covering leadership development through to budgeting and club finances.
A showcase event, to establish the club's presence on campus.
At least four members of the executive board complete Student Leader Orientation (SLO) in their first semester in office.
Annual re-recognition: the constitution is resubmitted through NYU Engage every year to keep the club active.
startingAnRso.note: Assembled from NYU's public SAB and Center for Student Life pages. The authoritative policies and the current NCD timeline live in the SAB Club Officer Handbook, which needs an NYU Home login — check the deadline there before relying on the September window. Individual schools run their own separate processes: Tandon, for example, registers clubs through its own student activities office rather than SAB.
